title: v1/chat.completions: reshape toolcall schema + streaming envelope stability and stop/role parity
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Customer integrations and SDKs expect /v1/chat.completions parity for structured function/tool calls, deterministic stop behavior, and stable streaming envelopes. This PR introduces a backward-compatible rewrite of the toolcall response schema, a role-normalizer pass for legacy role tokens, a deterministic stop-set reconciliation algorithm for multipart responses, and multiple streaming envelope stability fixes (heartbeat framing and chunk coalescing). Motivation: Reduce downstream parsing differences between Redwood's chatv1 adapter and OpenAI-style /v1/chat.completions to ease migration and reduce client-side parsing errors. Changes are scoped to the API adapter layer and streaming coordinator; runtime kernels are unchanged. Summary of changes: 1) Toolcall schema: replace ad-hoc tool output embedding with a first-class "agent_metadata" object that contains schema_version, tool_id, tool_signature, and structured_output_hints. Existing tool outputs are still emitted under "tool_output.payload.v1" for compatibility; new clients can consume the cleaner top-level shape. 2) Function/tool calling handshake: added a two-step handshake on stream start that emits a small metadata frame (frame_type: "handshake_meta") before any tokens to ensure SDKs can bind callbacks deterministically. 3) Streaming stability: introduced chunk coalescing for sub-10-byte fragments, improved backpressure handling in the stream coordinator, and added an idempotent heartbeat sentinel to help clients detect interrupted streams and resume parsing without duplicating tokens. 4) Stop/logprobs/roles parity: implemented a stop-set reconciliation pass that merges stop arrays coming from multiple fragments and a role_normalizer that maps legacy system/user/assistant aliases to canonical role names. 5) SDK tests and examples: updated Python/TS SDKs to show new schema consumption patterns and added integration tests that exercise partial stream resumes and toolcall parsing. Backwards compatibility: The adapter emits both legacy and new fields for 6 weeks behind a feature flag; the default rollout enables dual-output for all hosted customers, and Dedicated/Private customers can toggle via config. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for handshake and chunk coalescing - [x] Integration tests for toolcall schema migration - [x] SDK examples updated - [x] Load test for streaming coordinator under 10k rps - [x] Docs draft for API changes (docs PR linked) Related: DOCS-1912 (docs update), SDK-884 (TS example), SDK-889 (python integration).
commits: a1b2c3f: initial schema prototype and tests; d4e5f6a: add chunk coalescing and heartbeat sentinel; f7g8h9i: role normalizer + stop reconciliation; j1k2l3m: SDK examples and CI fixes; n4o5p6q: docs link and feature-flag gating
review_thread:
Reviewer Dmitri: Please confirm that emitting dual fields won't double-count tokens in billing.
Author Maya: The adapter emits the new top-level agent_metadata only for framing and does not duplicate token payloads; we added a billing regression test to ensure no double-count.
Reviewer Aisha: Can we avoid the extra handshake latency for low-latency customers?
Author Maya: Handshake frame is ~120 bytes and sent immediately; we added a config toggle that clients can opt out of for ultra-low latency flows.
Reviewer Rafael: The role normalizer mapping table looks permissive; can we make mappings explicit and documented?
Author Maya: Added explicit mapping table to docs and a config-driven allowlist; also added a unit test covering alias collision cases.
CI: initial pipeline failed due to linter in TS SDK; author fixed imports and retriggered; final CI run passed.
release_notes: Added a new toolcall response schema (agent_metadata) and handshake frame to improve OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity. Streaming envelope stability improved via heartbeat sentinels and chunk coalescing. Stop set merging and role normalization reduce client parsing differences. Dual-output compatibility mode enabled behind feature flag. See docs/openai_compat/v1_chat_completions.md for migration guidance.
